sections.h2: How big is Citrus County and who lives there?
sections.html:
Citrus County spans 581.92 land square miles, and its 2025 population estimate is 171,666, up 11.6% from 153,843 in 2020.

The age mix leans senior, with 38.1% at 65 or above and 14.2% under 18. Owners occupy 85.2% of the 90,919 housing units, and permits issued in 2025 numbered 2,102.

Median home value is $245,500 for 2020 to 2024, and owners pay a median of $1,354 a month with a mortgage or $447 without. Households bring in a median $56,546, and 13.5% of people live in poverty. Per capita income is $36,732 across 71,291 households of 2.24 people, and 15.6% of residents under 65 report a disability, so a tax bill matters to many fixed-income households.

sections.h2: Which Citrus County office does what?
sections.html:
Valuation and exemption rulings come from the property appraiser here, while the tax collector sends the bill, takes payment and sells certificates.

  • Property appraiser: homestead and other exemption applications, portability, agricultural classification and the August TRIM notice. The office phone is (352) 341-6600.
  • Tax collector: bills, discounts, installment applications and delinquent tax advertising.
  • Clerk: files the deed at closing and collects stamp tax.

The appraiser's site lists March 1 as the filing deadline for portability, exemptions, classifications and assessment reductions, with April 1 for tangible personal property. Owners who buy a home after January 1 are encouraged to pre-file for the next year.

sections.h2: What are the Citrus County tax discounts and due dates?
sections.html:
The 4% November discount is the best of the year; it falls by one point each month, and March carries the gross amount, due by March 31.

sections.h2: Can I pay Citrus County property tax in installments?
sections.html:
Quarterly payments are allowed. The application must reach the collector by April 30, and eligibility turns on prior year taxes above $100.

June 30 is the first due date, at 6% off, and a payment taken between July 1 and July 30 gets no discount. September 30 brings the second at 4.5% off and December 31 the third at 3% off. The fourth, due March 31, has no discount. If the first payment is missed, the plan ends and the full tax is due by March 31.

Payments one and two follow last year's bill. Ownership, value or exemption changes show up in payments three and four. The collector says enrolled taxpayers are re-enrolled automatically, so a buyer taking over a home with an active plan should ask the office what applies for that year, and a seller should say in the contract who owes which installment.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Citrus County taxes?
sections.html:
The bill is delinquent from April 1, with a 3% penalty on the gross amount.

In May the collector prints the delinquent list in the local newspaper weekly for three weeks, and that cost lands on the bill. Selling of certificates begins by June 1. Unpaid tangible personal property carries a 1.5% penalty after April 1 and is advertised once.

A holder can apply for a tax deed after two years from April 1 of the certificate's issue year. Redemption stays open until a deed issues, and the opening bid on a homestead parcel includes half the assessed value. Ask the collector for a payoff before listing.

sections.h2: How do homestead and Save Our Homes work for a Citrus County owner?
sections.html:
Homestead exemption can reach $50,000, and the Citrus County appraiser must receive your application by March 1 of the year you apply.

Per the appraiser's page, $25,000 reduces every tax, and a second $25,000 reduces only non-school taxes on assessed value over $50,000. The same page puts the typical savings at roughly $500 a year. After the first year, the assessment cannot rise by more than the lesser of CPI change or 3 percent. If you moved from one Florida homestead to another within three years, you may be able to take some of your Save Our Homes savings along.

State guidance says homestead ends if the owner rents the unit or stops living there permanently, and a sale resets value to just value the next January 1.

sections.h2: What does the Census show about work and housing in Citrus County?
sections.html:
Only 40.3% of people aged 16 and over are in the civilian labor force, and the county counts 17,659 veterans. Medical and social assistance receipts reached $1,111,065 thousand in 2022, and retail sales were $2,628,656 thousand, or $16,176 a resident.

There were 3,063 employer establishments and 31,162 paid employees in 2023, and workers average a 27.8 minute commute. Renters pay about $1,107, and 88.3% of residents stayed in their home through the past year. Another 13,125 nonemployer businesses operate here, which suggests many owners work from a home or small shop.

Rental owners should know that furniture and equipment used in a rental or business is taxed separately as tangible personal property. Returns are due April 1, and unpaid tangible tax carries a 1.5% penalty after April 1.

sections.h2: What changes for a Citrus County seller at closing?
sections.html:
The title company divides the year's tax between the parties and clears any back taxes out of your proceeds at the table.

The state's deed stamp tax runs 70 cents per $100 of consideration in most counties, collected at recording, and each party is liable whichever side agrees to pay. Citrus County's older, long-tenured owner base means many sellers hold capped assessments, so the buyer's first bill after a sale often looks different from the seller's last. Before closing, ask for three things.

  • A written payoff covering the current year and any earlier balance.
  • Word on whether a certificate was sold against the parcel.
  • The standing of any installment plan, which renews each year.

faqs.q: What is the Citrus County early payment discount?
faqs.a: The discount starts at 4% for November and drops by a point each month through February. Nothing comes off in March, and April 1 begins delinquency.

faqs.q: When is the installment application due in Citrus County?
faqs.a: Applications close April 30. The first payment is due June 30, and a payment in July earns no discount.

faqs.q: When does a Citrus County tax bill turn delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1, with a 3% penalty on the gross amount. A certificate sale starts by June 1.

faqs.q: What is the homestead filing deadline in Citrus County?
faqs.a: The appraiser must have the application by March 1 of the year you want it. That office, not the collector, decides eligibility.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Citrus County house that has delinquent tax?
faqs.a: Yes, because back taxes and fees are paid out of the proceeds at the table. Request a payoff before closing and ask whether a certificate was sold.
